cx_overview: Explore an unfamiliar directory or inspect a source file before editing: returns one directory level or a symbol outline with locations, without reading every body. Use path for the directory/file; omit it for the current project. For a known implementation use cx_definition; for full text/config use read. Output is bounded to 50KB/2000 lines.
cx_symbols: Locate the function, class, method or type you need to edit, even when you do not know its file. Returns matching symbols and source locations. Start with name='*Cache*' for discovery or an exact name for a known symbol; narrow with file/kind/scope. Scope matches the complete qualified name; use Parent::* for members. Requires a filter or kinds=true. Use grep for raw text rather than symbol lookup.
cx_definition: Read the implementation you need to understand or edit without paging through a whole source file. Supply the lexical name; use from (file) or scope to distinguish same-named methods. Returns bounded source bodies and locations; defaults to role=definition. Scope matches complete qualified names; Parent::* selects members. If the name is unknown, locate it with cx_symbols or cx_context first.
cx_references: Check uses of an identifier before renaming it or changing its behavior. Returns syntax-classified occurrences and locations; set context=true for surrounding source. Supply a lexical name such as load, not a qualified name. For callers of a particular method use cx_callers with scope. Matches are syntax evidence, not compiler-resolved identity.
cx_callers: Find which functions call a function or method before changing its interface or behavior. Returns direct caller sites with resolution evidence, candidates and unresolved targets. Supply a lexical name and optional complete qualified scope to narrow the target. For multiple reverse-call hops use cx_impact. Unresolved candidates are not proven calls.
cx_callees: Follow a function's implementation into the helpers it calls while investigating a bug. Returns direct callee sites with resolution evidence. Supply a lexical name and optional complete qualified scope. Ambiguous targets remain candidates rather than guessed identities; this is one hop, not a runtime trace.
cx_map: Get your bearings in an unfamiliar repository before choosing where to edit. Returns a bounded map of subsystems and import edges; depth controls detail. Use cx_overview for one directory/file or cx_context when you already have task keywords. Import warnings and ranking are retained; this is not a runtime dependency graph.
cx_refresh: Verify that navigation includes changed files when your next decision needs explicit index-generation proof. Pass changed paths; omit paths or use [] to verify the whole project. Ordinary queries already check freshness, so an explicit refresh is not required before every lookup.
cx_impact: Trace which callers could be affected by changing one function, across multiple reverse-call hops. Select one exact root with name plus file/scope/site selectors. Returns shortest supported and possible paths, unresolved frontiers, coverage and separate traversal/output limits. Use cx_callers for a direct caller list. Static evidence is not compiler/runtime proof or a safety verdict.
cx_changes: Review your edits with symbol context: compare tracked working files to HEAD, showing old/new symbols and file-level changes. Use staged=true for staged edits or base/head for commits; impact=true adds separate before/after call-impact analysis. Includes non-source changes. Does not run commands/tests or prove behavioral safety; untracked files are outside this comparison.
cx_context: Find where to make a requested change when you have task keywords but no file or symbol yet. Supply a short query using likely code identifiers, paths or English terms from the task; returns ranked source locations and bounded original excerpts. Set includeBody=true for implementation context. Matches exact names, paths, subwords and body/comment/string text: lexical retrieval, not semantic search. Use cx_definition once the symbol is known; use grep for exhaustive raw-text matches. Results and pagination are byte-bounded.
